evals.prompt: I'm planning a settings page for our SaaS app (profile, notifications, billing, team members, danger zone). Before we build it, can you prototype a few directions so I can feel which one works? Make it something I can open and play with.
evals.expected_output: Build mode, kind web. Writes prototypes/<slug>.parts.html with a manifest (id, name, brief, 3 structurally different variants with names and theses, e.g. single-column sections / tabbed / sidebar-nav + panels) and builds prototypes/<slug>.html via scripts/build-prototype.mjs, which validates with 0 errors. Sets manifest.dials to "standard" (a full page) and at most a couple of extraControls. Variants consume --pt-* tokens (no hardcoded colors/fonts/radii), use realistic settings content, render at 390 and 1280, and the handover message explains the Deck (arrows, presets, dials, pins, Export to LLM) and asks the user to paste the handoff back.

evals.prompt: We have a DESIGN.md in this repo from the design-creator skill. Prototype the new 'orders' dashboard home for the ops team: they need today's exceptions first, then the order queue, and a way to open one order. Two or three options please, and keep it on-brand.
evals.expected_output: Reads DESIGN.md and seeds manifest.defaults (accent hue/sat/light, neutral hue, display/body fonts, radius) and a brand preset from it. Variants differ structurally (exceptions-first KPI + table / queue-first ledger / split list + detail) and declare two screens (home, order) navigated with PT.go. Build + validate pass; the handover notes which values came from DESIGN.md.

evals.prompt: I'm writing a little terminal tool in Go with Bubble Tea to triage failing CI jobs. Can you mock up the TUI so the team can react to the layout before I code it? I'm torn between a split-pane view and a single pane with tabs.
evals.expected_output: Build mode, kind tui, controls tui. Two variants (split panes, tabbed) authored as <pre class="tui"> inside .tui-stage/.tui-window with single-line box glyphs, realistic CI job data, a key-hint bar, selection highlighting via .bg-sel and status colors via .ok/.warn/.err. Build + validate pass; handover mentions the Theme/Border glyphs/Columns dials and offers to scaffold Bubble Tea code after the handoff.

evals.prompt: Quick one: mock up the 'saved' toast for our app. I can't decide between an inline bar under the header and a little card in the corner with Undo. Brand look is fixed (Manrope, green accent), I just want to see the two shapes side by side.
evals.expected_output: Build mode, small scope. Two structurally different variants (inline bar, corner card). Right-sizes the Deck: manifest.dials is "none" (or "essential" at most, with fontDisplay/fontBody locked via hideControls), brand values seeded in defaults (fontDisplay/fontBody Manrope, accentHue green), no extraControls beyond what the question needs. Build + validate pass with 0 errors. The handover describes only what the Deck has (flip variants, widths, light/dark, pins, Export) instead of promising presets and sliders that are not there.

evals.prompt: Our design lead wants to explore a new visual direction for the whole marketing site: warmer, more editorial, maybe a serif. Build a prototype of the homepage she can really tune: fonts, weights, tracking, line height, contrast, everything, plus a dark-first pass.
evals.expected_output: Build mode, large scope. Variants explore structure (narrative scroll, split hero, editorial long-form). manifest.dials is "full" because the user explicitly wants every typographic and color knob; a brand preset and a dark preset are added; any custom controls are few and structural (e.g. hero media style). Build + validate pass; the handover names the Feel macros and the Type/Color groups and asks for the handoff back.
